details:
dynamic-mcp presents itself as an MCP server for crash-dump and kernel analysis (wrapping the crash utility and bpftrace). Every version, by default, opens a public Cloudflare quick tunnel to an unauthenticated HTTP server on the user's machine and reports the tunnel URL to a host the publisher controls, giving whoever holds that URL the server's tools; from 1.0.4 the tools include arbitrary command execution (bash -c) with the user's privileges. The README describes only local stdio and HTTP use and mentions none of this.

Trigger: launching the server (dynamic-mcp or dynamic-mcp-http; the CLI has no --help path, so dynamic-mcp --help launches it too), unless ENABLE_REVERSE_CONNECTION is set to false.

Lines below are from 1.0.9 (sdist sha256 cebb5d206b015b1b851121e31946f5a0a0b42daa697cfece1429d6f396623179):
- src/dynamic_mcp/server.py:1489-1490 sets ENABLE_REVERSE_CONNECTION=true when it is not set, turning the tunnel on by default
- src/dynamic_mcp/server.py:1530-1552 starts the HTTP server on 0.0.0.0:8080 unless --stdio is given
- src/dynamic_mcp/tunnel_manager.py:83-104 downloads cloudflared from the cloudflare/cloudflared latest GitHub release into ~/.local/bin/cloudflared, with no version pin or checksum
- src/dynamic_mcp/tunnel_manager.py:126-131 runs cloudflared tunnel --url http://localhost:<port>
- src/dynamic_mcp/server.py:1387-1406 POSTs the server name, capabilities and tunnel URL to https://production.dynamic-agent.workers.dev/api/mcp/connect, and server.py:1409-1432 sends a heartbeat there every 20 seconds
- src/dynamic_mcp/server.py:989-1080 dispatches /api/mcp/request calls straight to the tool handlers with no authentication, and server.py:643-680 runs bash -c <command> and returns its output

History: 0.2.0 (2025-12-28) through 0.3.4 already open the tunnel by default and register the URL with https://dynamic.artem-blagodarenko.workers.dev, exposing the crash and bpftrace tools; 1.0.4 (2026-07-25) adds bash -c execution; 1.0.6 onward register with production.dynamic-agent.workers.dev.

Found by Bitbison (https://bitbison.io) in its registry's backfill of packages already on PyPI, which builds each release in a sandbox and records what it does; a review confirming it from the source was published on 2026-11-06. The package has opened the tunnel by default since its first version, 2025-12-28 (about ten months), and exposed command execution since 1.0.4, 2026-07-25 (about three and a half months), with no report; pypistats counts 1,172 downloads in the last 180 days.

files.note: cloudflared downloaded and run to open the tunnel
